auth.bad_key_prefix: {env} does not look like a Listo API key.
auth.grant_unavailable: This build cannot use the saved login.
auth.live_key_needs_flag: This is a live API key, but live mode was not selected.
auth.next_drop_live: Remove --live, or use a live key (it starts with lst_live_).
auth.next_key_prefix: A key starts with lst_test_ or lst_live_. Copy it from the developer dashboard.
auth.no_live_session: No live session on this computer.
auth.test_key_with_live: This is a test API key, but --live was given.
completion.example:
listo completion bash > /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/listo
  listo completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_listo"
  listo completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/listo.fish
completion.long: Prints a completion script for your shell. Load it once from your shell profile to complete commands and flags.
completion.next_shells: Use bash, zsh, fish or powershell.
config.unavailable: Could not open the configuration folder ({detail}).
config.unreadable: Could not read the saved login ({detail}).
confirm.needs_terminal: This action needs your confirmation and there is no terminal to ask on.
deliveries.bad_json: The order is not a valid JSON object ({detail}).
deliveries.cancel_example:
listo deliveries cancel dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe --reason store_closed
  listo deliveries cancel dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe --live
deliveries.create_example:
listo deliveries create --data @order.json
  cat order.json | listo deliveries create
  listo deliveries create --live --data @order.json
deliveries.create_long:
Sends your JSON to POST /v1/deliveries as it is; the API checks it. An Idempotency-Key is made for the call and printed, so sending the same call again does not book a second courier (use --idempotency-key to send your own).

With --live the CLI first asks the API for a quote for the same store and drop-off, tells you the store, the address and the delivery fee, and on y books that quote, so the amount you saw is the amount charged.
deliveries.create_short: Create a delivery from a JSON file or standard input
deliveries.example:
listo deliveries create --data @order.json
  listo deliveries get dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe
  listo deliveries cancel dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe --reason store_closed
deliveries.flag_data: The order as JSON: @file.json, @- for standard input, or the JSON itself
deliveries.flag_description: A sentence of explanation (needed when the reason is other; default: a note that it came from the CLI)
deliveries.flag_idempotency_key: Idempotency-Key to send (default: a new one for each call)
deliveries.get_example:
listo deliveries get dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe
  listo deliveries get dlv_7hK2mQ9xR4tV6bN1cZ8sLwYe --json
deliveries.get_long: Reads GET /v1/deliveries/{id}. Prints the delivery as JSON when piped or with --json.
deliveries.long: Create a delivery from your own JSON, read one by its id, or cancel one. In test mode nothing real happens. With --live these book and cancel real couriers, and ask you first.
deliveries.next_bad_json: Fix the JSON and run the command again.
deliveries.next_missing_store: Add store_id to the order. Your stores are listed by GET /v1/stores.
deliveries.next_no_order: Pass --data @order.json, or pipe the JSON in.
deliveries.payer_split: of which the store pays {store} and the customer {customer}
deliveries.watch: Run listo listen to watch it.
deliveries.will_book: This will book a courier for "{store}" ({store_id}) to {address}, delivery fee {fee} {payer}.
deliveries.will_book_balance: This will book a courier for "{store}" ({store_id}) to {address}, delivery fee {fee} {payer}, from your live balance.
deliveries.will_cancel: This will cancel {id} ({code}), which is {status}. Canceling after a courier was already working on the order is billed as a cancellation fee: cancellation charges depend on how far the trip had progressed and are posted to your balance as a separate ledger entry.
error.bad_arguments: The arguments do not match what this command takes.
error.bad_lang: '{value}' is not a language the CLI has.
error.label: Error:
error.next.idempotency_conflict: Use a new idempotency key, or send the same body again.
error.next.insufficient_balance: Add balance in the dashboard and try again.
error.next.invalid_api_key: Run listo login, or check the key in LISTO_API_KEY.
error.next.plan_required: Choose a plan in the dashboard and try again.
error.next.rate_limited: Wait a moment and try again.
error.next.read_only_key: Use a key that is not read-only, or run listo login.
error.next.test_webhook_limit: Wait a moment before triggering another test event.
error.next_network: Check your connection and try again.
flag.json: Print JSON instead of text (always on when the output is not a terminal)
flag.lang: Output language, es or en (default: your computer's language)
flag.live: Use live mode (real money). Test mode is the default
listen.bad_url: {url} is not a web address listen can send to.
listen.catch_up_failed: Reconnected, but could not read the events missed while offline ({detail}).
listen.closed_by_server: The server closed the connection and asked not to reconnect ({reason}).
listen.example:
listo listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks/listo
  listo listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks/listo --events delivery.status_changed,delivery.rated
  listo listen --print-secret
listen.flag_events: Only send these event types (comma separated)
listen.flag_forward_to: Web address on your computer to send each event to
listen.flag_print_secret: Print the webhook signing secret and exit
listen.long:
Opens a live connection to your account and sends every event to a web address on your computer, signed so your webhook handler can verify it exactly as it does in production. No public address is needed.

The signing secret is made once for this computer and does not change between runs. Set it as LISTO_WEBHOOK_SECRET in your app.
listen.need_forward_to: Tell listen where to send the events.
listen.next_bad_url: Use a full address that starts with http:// or https://.
listen.next_key_revoked: Create a new API key on the developer dashboard, or run listo login.
listen.next_key_revoked_live: Create a new live API key on the developer dashboard, or run listo login --live.
listen.next_try_again: Try again in a moment, or run listo login.
listen.rate_limited: Too many connection attempts. Waiting {seconds} s before trying again.
listen.ready: Ready {badge}. Your webhook signing secret is {secret} (set LISTO_WEBHOOK_SECRET in your app)
listen.short: Receive your webhook events on your computer
listen.subscription_rejected: The server did not accept the connection to your live stream.
login.browser_failed: Could not open the browser. Open the address above yourself.
login.complete_needs_code: --complete needs the device code that listo login --non-interactive printed.
login.denied: The request was not allowed on the page.
login.done_key: Done. This computer will use the {mode} API key of {partner}.
login.done_live: Done. This computer is "{device}" in Live mode. Run listo login to add Test.
login.done_test: Done. This computer is "{device}" in Test mode. Run listo login --live to add Live.
login.example:
listo login
  listo login --live
  listo login --key lst_test_...
  listo login --non-interactive
  listo login --complete lso_dc_...
login.expired: The code expired before it was approved.
login.flag_complete: Finish a login started with --non-interactive, using the device code it printed
login.flag_key: Save an API key (lst_test_... or lst_live_...) instead of signing in with the browser
login.flag_non_interactive: Print the code and the address as JSON and exit (finish with --complete)
login.long:
Opens your browser so you can approve this computer on the developer dashboard. Test mode is the default; add --live to approve Live too. Each mode keeps its own login.

With no terminal (a script, a container) it prints the code and the address as JSON and exits; finish it from another shell with --complete. You can also save an API key from the dashboard with --key.
login.mode_differs: Note: you asked for {asked} mode, and the page approved {got} mode.
login.no_login_host: The sign-in address cannot be worked out from {api}.
login.press_enter: Press Enter to open {url} in your browser (or open it yourself). Compare the code on the page with the one above before you authorize.
login.rejected: The sign-in host refused the request ({detail}).
login.save_failed: Could not save the login on this computer ({detail}).
login.short: Log in to your Listo account
login.stored_file: Saved in {path}, because no system credential store answered.
login.stored_keyring: Saved in your system credential store.
login.unknown_mode: The API answered with a mode the CLI does not know ({mode}).
logout.done: Logged out of {mode} mode on this computer.
logout.env_note: {env} is still set in your environment.
logout.key_note: The key itself still works. Revoke it on the developer dashboard if you no longer want it.
logout.long: Ends the login of the selected mode (Test, or Live with --live): the session is revoked on the server, and the login and the webhook signing secret are removed from this computer. A saved API key is only forgotten here.
logout.nothing: Nothing to log out of in {mode} mode.
logout.server_unreachable: Could not reach the server to end the session there ({detail}). The login was removed from this computer; remove the connection on the developer dashboard to be sure.
logs.example:
listo logs tail
  listo logs tail --status failed
logs.flag_all: Also show the reads this tool makes itself to catch up
logs.flag_endpoint: Only requests to this endpoint, for example api/v1/deliveries#create
logs.flag_status: Only failed (status 400 or above) or succeeded requests
logs.long: Commands that read your /v1/ request log.
logs.ready: Following the request log {badge}. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
logs.tail_example:
listo logs tail
  listo logs tail --status failed
  listo logs tail --endpoint api/v1/deliveries#create
logs.tail_long:
Opens a live connection to your account and prints one line per /v1/ request: time, method, path, status, duration, error code and request id.

The reads this tool makes itself to catch up after a lost connection are hidden unless you add --all.
logs.tail_short: Print each API request as it happens
root.example:
listo login
  listo listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhooks/listo
  listo trigger delivery.status_changed
  listo logs tail
root.long:
Log in, receive your webhooks on your computer, trigger test events, tail your API logs and create deliveries, all from the terminal.

Test mode is the default. Live mode needs --live and a confirmation before anything is written.
root.short: Command-line tool for the Listo Delivery API
simulate.example:
listo simulate returned
  listo simulate no_courier --store st_4bR8kM2wQ7xT1nV5cZ9pLdYe
simulate.flag_store: The st_ id of the test store to use (default: your first test store)
simulate.next_no_store: Create one with POST /v1/stores (see https://docs.listo.delivery/en/quickstart), then run listo simulate again.
simulate.no_store: This account has no test store yet.
simulate.refused_live: Simulations only run with a test key, because they play a courier that does not exist.
simulate.short: Play a courier scenario on a test delivery
trigger.confirm_live_deliver: This will send a test {type} event to your live webhook URL.
trigger.confirm_live_listen: This will record a test {type} event on your live account and show it to your listen sessions. Nothing is posted to your webhook URL.
trigger.example:
listo trigger delivery.status_changed
  listo trigger delivery.status_changed --deliver
  listo trigger store.updated --json
trigger.flag_deliver: Also POST the event to your webhook URL
trigger.long:
Sends a sample event of one type, marked test: true, to the sessions running listo listen. Nothing is posted to your webhook URL unless you add --deliver. Event types:
{list}
trigger.sent: Sent {id} (test: true) to your listen sessions. Add --deliver to also POST it to your webhook URL.
trigger.sent_delivered: Sent {id} (test: true) to your listen sessions and queued it for your webhook URL.
trigger.unknown_event: '{type}' is not an event type Listo sends.
update.available: A new version is available: {latest} (you have {current}). Run listo update to install it.
update.check_failed: Could not check for a new version ({detail}).
update.download_failed: Could not download the update ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
update.flag_check: Only check whether a new version exists; install nothing
update.long:
Installs the newest release when listo was installed with the install script. A copy installed with npm or Homebrew is updated with that tool, and this command prints the right command for it.

The download is checked against the release signing key and its checksum before anything is replaced.
update.next_network: Check your connection and try again.
update.next_retry: Nothing was changed. Try again, and if it keeps failing reinstall with the install script.
update.no_signing_key: This build has no release signing key, so it cannot verify an update.
update.not_script: listo was not installed with the install script, so it cannot update itself. Update it the way you installed it, or reinstall with: {command}
update.notice: A new version of listo is available: {latest} (you have {current}). Upgrade with: {command}
update.notice_unknown: A new version of listo is available: {latest} (you have {current}). How to upgrade: {url}
update.package_manager: listo was installed with {manager}. Update it with: {command}
update.short: Update listo to the newest release
update.verify_failed: The update did not pass verification ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
update.write_failed: Could not replace the listo binary ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
usage.more: Run "{command} [command] --help" for more about a command.
whoami.example:
listo whoami
  listo whoami --live
  listo whoami --json
whoami.long: Asks the API which company the credential belongs to and which mode it acts in.
whoami.short: Show who you are logged in as
